name: Ayonga Hereid
role: Associate Professor; Principal Investigator, Cyberbotics Lab
research: Physical intelligence for humanoid robots: reinforcement learning, nonlinear control, trajectory optimization and motion planning for perceptive locomotion, autonomous navigation, whole-body control and safe learning, tested on humanoid and lower-limb exoskeleton platforms. NSF CAREER Award (2022) for hierarchical RL for safe bipedal locomotion. Open-source FROST framework.
alignment: Closest match. Om's Omnix hexapod (gaits, IMU sensing), Whispering Hat (assistive wearable) and robotCar (autonomous navigation) map directly onto legged locomotion, exoskeleton/assistive robotics and perception-based navigation. Shared tools: Python, C++, simulation, RL.
verification: Email listed on official MAE profile (page updated Oct 29, 2026)
notes: MAE's robotics listing still shows 'Assistant Professor'; his own profile says Associate Professor. Lab site: cyberboticslab.com

name: Manoj Srinivasan
research: Theory of human and animal movement and sensorimotor control, using mathematics, modeling, computation and experiments: energy-optimal locomotion, stability and control, design of wearable robotics (prostheses, exoskeletons). Some current work overlaps with human and robot learning and cognition. NSF CAREER recipient.
alignment: Strong match for Omnix (walking gaits, IMU feedback) and for the assistive-device angle of the Whispering Hat. Om's strong math record (MATHCOUNTS, MOEMS) suits this lab's modeling-and-optimization style.
verification: Email listed on official MAE robotics faculty page
notes: Lab page: mae.osu.edu/movement. Most recent publications not reviewed.

name: Debdipta Goswami
role: Assistant Professor (joint appointment, MAE and ECE)
department: Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering; Electrical and Computer Engineering
research: Control systems plus machine learning: data-driven discovery and control of dynamical systems (operator-theoretic methods, reservoir computing), learning of control systems from data with performance guarantees, and model predictive control and motion planning for aerial robots (UAVs).
alignment: Good match for Ringwraith (home-built quadcopter, Betaflight/ExpressLRS) combined with Om's ML experience; the lab pairs drones with learning-based control.
verification: Email listed on official MAE profile (page updated Oct 6, 2026)
notes: Joined OSU in 2022. Research webpage: goswami78.github.io

name: Wei-Lun (Harry) Chao
role: Associate Professor with tenure (promoted May 2025); College of Engineering Innovation Scholar; advisor, OSU AI Club and Buckeye AutoDrive Team
research: Machine learning and computer vision: learning from imperfect data (limited, noisy, shifted distributions), interpretable and personalized ML, robust perception for autonomous driving, visual recognition in the wild, with applications in biology and health. Member of the ICICLE and Imageomics NSF institutes. 2025 OSU Early Career Distinguished Scholar Award.
alignment: Strong match for robotCar and Whispering Hat (OpenCV/computer-vision perception) and for TankFlare-style ML on biological data. His AI Club and AutoDrive student teams are a realistic first point of contact for a young student.
verification: Email listed on his official homepage and TDAI directory

name: Tanya Berger-Wolf

department: Computer Science and Engineering; Electrical and Computer Engineering; Evolution, Ecology and Organismal Biology
research: Computational ecology and imageomics: machine learning on images of living organisms to extract biological traits; AI for biodiversity and conservation (AI for Biodiversity Change global climate center); co-founder of the Wild Me / Wildbook conservation-AI project. alignment: Natural bridge from TankFlare (random-forest fish/plant compatibility model) and the allergy predictor (sensor and environmental ML) to applied data science for nature. TDAI is also the hub for data-science programs at OSU.
